{{Use British English|date=October 2026}}

{{Short description|British supramolecular chemist}}

'''Anthony P. Davis''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry|FRSC]] is a British chemist currently serving as Professor of [[Supramolecular chemistry|Supramolecular Chemistry]] at the [[University of Bristol]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony P Davis |url=https://research-information.bris.ac.uk/en/persons/anthony-p-davis/ |access-date=2026-10-17 |website=[[University of Bristol]] |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name="Journal-1">{{Cite journal |date=2010 |title=Author profile: Anthony P. Davis |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/anie.200905858 |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition |volume=49 |issue=1 |pages=26–26 |doi=10.1002/anie.200905858 |issn=1521-3773|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Davis was born 27th August 1954.<ref name="Journal-1" /> He enrolled at the [[University of Oxford]] in 1973,<ref name="Journal-1" /> graduating with a BA in chemistry in 1977,<ref name="Website-1">{{Cite web |title=Professor Anthony P Davis {{!}} Davis Research Group |url=https://davis.chm.bris.ac.uk/prof-anthony-p-davis/ |access-date=2026-10-17 |website=davis.chm.bris.ac.uk |language=en-US}}</ref> and from 1977 to 1979 studied for a [[Doctor of Philosophy|D. Phil]] under [[Gordon Whitham|G.H. Whitham]].<ref name="Journal-1" /> His thesis was entitled ''Synthetic aspects of organosulphur chemistry''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Davis |first=Anthony Peter |date=1980 |title=Synthetic aspects of organosulphur chemistry |url=https://solo.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/discovery/fulldisplay?docid=alma990169232910107026&context=L&vid=44OXF_INST:SOLO&lang=en&search_scope=MyInst_and_CI&adaptor=Local%20Search%20Engine&tab=Everything&query=any,contains,anthony%20davis&facet=searchcreationdate,include,1977%7C,%7C1980&facet=topic,include,Alkenes%20Synthesis&offset=0 |access-date=2026-10-17 |website=[[Bodleian Library]] |language=en}}</ref>

== Career ==
After graduating, Davis worked as a postdoctoral researcher at Oxford under [[Jack Baldwin (chemist)|J.E. Baldwin]] from 1979 to 1981, when he left to take up a Royal Society European exchange Fellowship at [[ETH Zurich]] under [[Albert Eschenmoser]]. In 1982, he began work at [[Trinity College Dublin]]<ref name="Journal-1" /> as a lecturer in organic chemistry,<ref name="Website-1" /> where he remained until 2000, and has worked at the [[University of Bristol]] since.<ref name="Journal-1" />

Davis serves as chair of the editorial board for the [[Royal Society of Chemistry|RSC]] journal ''[[Organic and Biomolecular Chemistry]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Organic & Biomolecular Chemistry |url=https://pubs.rsc.org/ob |access-date=17 October 2026 |website=[[Royal Society of Chemistry]]}}</ref>

Davis has co-founded two [[Startup company|startup companies]] to develop practical applications for his work: Zylo in 2014 and Carbometrics in 2018.<ref name="Website-1" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony DAVIS personal appointments - Find and update company information - GOV.UK |url=https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/officers/Gx_9pkki56ccQ31mwuEGxFkchPs/appointments |access-date=2026-10-17 |website=[[Companies House]] |language=en}}</ref>

== Recognition ==
Davis received the 2002 [[Tilden Prize]] of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] and was the 2003 [[Abbott Laboratories]] Distinguished Lecturer.<ref name="Journal-1" /> He received the RSC Robert Robinson Award in 2020<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Anthony Davis |url=https://www.rsc.org/standards-and-recognition/prizes/winners/professor-anthony-davis |access-date=2026-10-17 |website=Royal Society of Chemistry |language=en}}</ref> and the [[Royal Medal]] of the [[Royal Society]] in 2025 for designing artificial [[glucose]] receptor GluHUT to act as an in vitro glucose sensor and improve treatment of [[diabetes]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 August 2025 |title=Prestigious Royal Society award for Bristol scientist behind glucose-binding breakthrough |url=https://www.bristol.ac.uk/news/2025/august/anthony-davis-royal-medal.html |access-date=17 October 2026 |website=[[University of Bristol]]}}</ref>
